proof-statement-integrity.evidence: lean/QOU/TopologicalMass/cat_eigenspace_decomposition.lean did not derive the decomposition. CatEigenspaceDecompositionContext carried the conclusion as the field "decomposition" and the theorem body was ctx.decomposition, under a docstring asserting the body was an honest sorry (3b-cond item 5). Sharper point: alpha, tau_hat, tr, nrm and m_rho were ALL fields, so the instance chose them - and nrm : R -> R is an arbitrary function, nothing making it a norm, sub-additive or even non-negative, tr likewise. So the equation was not a claim about traces and norms but about three unconstrained functions. The file had also been repaired once before: its own notes record that the prior version laundered alpha = alpha_descended + alpha_transient through a fictitious intermediate_sum.
proof-statement-integrity.notes: Repaired to 1a disposition 3, and the two halves are now separated. split_eq states the algebraic identity alpha = tau(alpha) + (alpha - tau(alpha)) AS A TAUTOLOGY - it holds for every tau whatever - because that is exactly what the pre-repair version laundered as the lemmas content; naming it trivial is what stops it being mistaken for the claim again. transient_antiInvariant is real derived content: given tau additive on differences and involutive, the transient component lies in the -1 eigenspace, tau(alpha - tau alpha) = -(alpha - tau alpha). That is the eigenspace statement the lemma name promises, sorry-free and independent of any norm. Verdict major not critical: the eigenspace half is derived. Still open: norm-additivity (Pythagoras for the star-compatible Frobenius pairing) is the whole content and cannot even be stated honestly while nrm is an arbitrary function - it is a claim about a norm INDUCED by a pairing, and no pairing is constructed. Verified lean-direct exit 0. Bean qou-z9ws.
